title: Past the length ceiling means two ideas
statement: Treat a teaching piece that runs past the length ceiling for its kind of idea as a sign that it merges two ideas or is padded.
example: One rubric reads a single-fact script of over 280 words as a risk of silently merging two ideas.
detail: The evaluator's script rubric sets word bands for each kind of idea, computed in code after the model scores: a single-fact script over 280 words risks silently merging two ideas, and a mechanism script over 480 is likely teaching more than one (`shadow/bench/src/inceptbench/prompts/video_script/evaluation.txt` lines 409-423). The lower ends of the bands were later made advisory, one of three changes to stop the rubric false-failing correct short scripts; only going over the ceiling, or under an absolute minimum of 40 words, still scores zero (git commit 4ce0f47 in `shadow/bench`, lines 3-9). Don't fail a piece only for falling short of its target length.
against: The ceiling depends on judging the kind of idea, and that misfired: a 310-word script on a food web or a respiration loop was classed as a single fact and failed the 280-word ceiling until the keyword list was widened (git commit 2d26518 in `shadow/bench`, lines 3-8). The rubric's reason for its lower bound is an impression that such scripts feel abrupt, not a measurement (`video_script/evaluation.txt` line 422).

evidence.quote: - Over 280: risk of silently merging two KCs, or redundant elaboration that pads length without adding learning
- Over 480: likely teaching more than one mechanism, or padding with tangential content
This metric is computed deterministically by the evaluation system after LLM scoring.
1. length_discipline floor is now ADVISORY, not a binary zero. Being under the per-type word target no longer fails the metric; only over-ceiling (silent KC-merge risk)
